description: Single-panel weak-beam dark-field (WBDF) TEM micrograph of a dissociated dislocation in the base alloy, rendered in grey-scale over a dark, low-contrast austenite matrix; several fainter dislocation lines cross the upper part of the field. One prominent curved dislocation runs from mid-left toward the lower right; along it two overlapping white arrows with the label "d" mark the separation between the two partial dislocations, and an arc with the label "α" marks the character angle between the dislocation line vector and the Burgers vector. A white arrow labelled "g//b" points up-and-right, indicating that the two-beam g vector is parallel to the Burgers vector b of the undissociated dislocation. A boxed scale bar at bottom right reads "50 nm". A square inset at top right is a diffraction pattern with one strong central spot and a few faint satellite spots. No numeric values for d or α are printed anywhere in the figure. The panel illustrates how the paired (d, α) measurements that are fed into Eq. (1) to obtain stacking fault energy values were made.
measured_quantities: stacking fault energy (mJ m-2, computed from d and α via Eq. (1), not shown in the figure)

observations.observation: The figure is a grey-scale WBDF TEM micrograph of a dislocation in a dark, low-contrast matrix, with the dislocation imaged as a bright curved line.
A boxed scale bar in the bottom right corner of the micrograph is labelled "50 nm".
The annotation "g//b" with a white arrow marks the direction in which the diffraction vector g is parallel to the Burgers vector b of the undissociated dislocation.
An arrow labelled "d" together with an arc labelled "α" are drawn on the dislocation to define the partial dislocation separation d and the character angle α.
A square inset at the top right of the micrograph shows a diffraction pattern with a strong central spot and a few faint satellite spots.
No numerical values of d or α are printed on the figure; only the 50 nm scale bar carries a number.
The caption states that the image is a WBDF TEM micrograph of a dissociated dislocation in the base alloy and that the annotations are explained in the text.
The citing text states that multiple data pairs of partial dislocation separation d and perfect dislocation character angle α were recorded along several dislocations for each material.
The citing text states that α is the angle between the line vector and the Burgers vector b of the undissociated dislocation.

The citing text states that both partial dislocations are in contrast in the condition shown and that g·b_p analysis was performed, so the g vector used to form the two-beam condition is parallel to the undissociated dislocation Burgers vector b.
The citing text states that the paired (d, α) data were inserted into Eq. (1) to calculate stacking fault energy values for each measured data pair.

subfigures.description: Weak-beam dark-field TEM micrograph of a dissociated dislocation in the base alloy. A bright curved dislocation line runs from mid-left to lower right, with two overlapping white arrows along the line labelled "g//b"; an arc labelled "α" spans the character angle, and a white arrow labelled "d" indicates the partial separation. A boxed scale bar reading "50 nm" sits at the bottom right. Fainter dislocation lines are visible in the upper part of the field; many other lines are straight, near-vertical or near-horizontal segments.

Square inset showing a diffraction pattern: one strong central spot plus a few faint satellite spots; individual reflections are not annotated and are only partially resolvable at the supplied resolution.
